review_notes: I read the whole file and checked Mathlib's DirectSum.coeFnAddMonoidHom and its simp lemma. I also checked Representation.directSum for DecidableEq assumptions, and searched the formal-frontier sources for uses of the simp lemmas. I did not run Lean. The two findings are about the simp-normal form of the lemma statements. The `discreteDirectSum_V` and `discreteTensor_V` simp lemmas rewrite a carrier type; I found no concrete misuse of them and did not report them. The tensor section's simp lemmas look fine.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem discreteDirectSum_ρ_apply (g : G) (x : ⨁ i, X i) (i : ι) :
    (DirectSum.coeFnAddMonoidHom (fun i => X i) ((discreteDirectSum X).ρ g x)) i =
      (X i).ρ g (x i) := by
findings.problem: The `@[simp]` lemma has its left side written with the explicit bundled coercion `DirectSum.coeFnAddMonoidHom ... (…) i`. Mathlib's simp lemma `DirectSum.coeFnAddMonoidHom_apply` rewrites `coeFnAddMonoidHom β v` to `v`. The left side is therefore not in simp normal form, and the simp set will normalise a goal to the plain application `((discreteDirectSum X).ρ g x) i` before this lemma can match. The attribute is probably inert. The file shows the same mismatch: `discreteDirectSum_fixed_iff` has to `simpa only [DirectSum.coeFnAddMonoidHom_apply, h]` to bridge it by hand. The tensor and `of` lemmas in this file are stated in simp-normal form, so this one is inconsistent with them.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma without the bundled hom, as `((discreteDirectSum X).ρ g x) i = (X i).ρ g (x i)`. The coercion `⇑x i` is the normal form that `coeFnAddMonoidHom_apply` produces. The `rfl` proof should still work, since `coeFnAddMonoidHom_apply` is proved by `rfl`. Then `discreteDirectSum_fixed_iff` can use `(discreteDirectSum_ρ_apply X g x i)` directly, without `coeFnAddMonoidHom_apply`.
findings.benefit: `simp` will actually use the lemma on goals like `((discreteDirectSum X).ρ g x) i`. Users get a working coordinate-evaluation simp lemma, and the proof of `discreteDirectSum_fixed_iff` becomes simpler.

findings.excerpt:
open scoped Classical in
/-- Acting on a direct-sum injection commutes with that injection. -/
@[simp] theorem discreteDirectSum_ρ_of (g : G) (i : ι) (a : X i) :
findings.problem: The simp lemma is stated with `open scoped Classical`, so `DirectSum.of` in its left side uses the classical `DecidableEq ι` instance. `DirectSum.of` takes a `DecidableEq ι` argument. The lemma will therefore not match terms built with another instance, such as the standard instance for `ι = ℕ` or `Fin n`, up to simp's instance-reducibility. The statement does not need classical logic, because `Representation.directSum` is defined without any `DecidableEq` hypothesis. The lemma is the only way `simp` can compute the action on `of`, so it is limited by this choice.
findings.proposed_change: Add `[DecidableEq ι]` as an instance argument to the section variables or to this lemma, and drop `open scoped Classical in`. Inside the proofs of the other declarations, the existing `classical` calls can stay, since they would unify with the supplied instance when it is a variable. This is the standard Mathlib pattern for `DirectSum.of` lemmas.
findings.benefit: The simp lemma can fire for any decidable-equality instance on the index type, so users with concrete index types do not have to rewrite their `DirectSum.of` terms to the classical instance first.
